newsitem.title: CHINA: China should intensify medical reform - paper.
newsitem.headline: China should intensify medical reform - paper.

text.p: China should adopt a medical insurance plan and reform the current system of state-funded care to meet rising costs and stave off social unrest in its ailing state sector, the China Women's News said on Thursday.

China's health care costs were growing by 20-30 percent a year, faster than the national economy, and putting medical treatment out of reach for many people such as redundant state workers, the newspaper said in an editorial.

Millions of workers in China's inefficient and struggling state industries have been sent home from their posts, nominally retaining their jobs and a fraction of their salaries while losing many benefits such as cradle-to-grave health care.

A recent survey of 210,000 people by the Ministry of Public Health showed that 57.1 percent of those who got sick did not bother to seek treatment because medical costs were too high, the newspaper said.
"The problem of people not being able to afford medical fees is being a big problem which is connected to social stability," it said.
China's communist rulers are afraid that worker unrest sparked by painful, market-style economic reforms in the state sector could threaten its grip on power.
Rising health costs also meant China must reform its medical system and control total health expenditures, the newspaper said.
"Insurance should be introduced into health care and the system of the state guaranteeing medical costs of state workers should be changed," it said.
The state should try to clean up the "chaotic" situation in the pharmaceutical market by exercising macro-control over medicine prices, it said without elaborating.
